summary: Intel RST RAID metadata present on returned drives blocks Autopilot/SCCM provisioning
description:
Issue summary: Several depot-returned machines fail during Autopilot/SCCM provisioning because the drives contain leftover Intel RST/RAID metadata (RST ID header) from previous consumer RAID configurations. The imaging task sequence detects unexpected disk signature/metadata and drops into a manual recovery step, which blocks large batches and causes a backlog in the staging depot.

Impact: Affected devices cannot complete automated provisioning (Autopilot join + SCCM task sequence). Approx 12 units identified in the last 72 hours across two batches. This creates delays for new-assignee device fulfillment and increases depot manual triage time. No customer-facing outage; internal operational impact only.

Environment: Depot staging imaging farm (staging-us-west), standard offline task sequence v2026.02. Datacenter: us-west-1. Boot mode UEFI, BitLocker/TPM enabled on target images.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a drive that previously had consumer RAID metadata (intel RST) present (e.g., pulled from consumer laptop or testbench with RAID enabled).
2) Boot into provisioning PXE/WinPE and start SCCM task sequence / Autopilot offline registration step.
3) Task sequence fails at disk partitioning step (DiskPart / Clear not idempotent) or the Autopilot prepare script detects mismatched signature and aborts.
4) Imaging logs show warnings about 'Intel RST metadata header present' and DiskPart returns error 0x00000005 during clean.

Observed logs / artifacts:
- WinPE DISM logs and SMSTS logs attached to ticket (see linked GH PR for helper script).
- Sample SMSTS log excerpt: "DiskPart: cannot clear disk - Intel RST metadata detected (hdr 0x52)"
- Device inventory note: original serials indicate these drives were swapped during depot RMA repair and were not zeroed.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: Depot repair workflow sometimes returns drives that still contain Intel RST metadata. Standard 'clean' in our TS doesn't detect/overwrite the special RST headers reliably.
- Reproduced locally on a test drive with RST metadata. Running 'cryptic' vendor tool (Intel RST CLI) clears header and subsequent imaging completes.
- Workaround discovered: run a low-level wipe command (sgdisk --zap-all or vendor RST clear tool) in WinPE prior to partitioning, or use 'clean all' (slow).
- Risk: 'clean all' increases imaging time per device (30+ minutes) and is not acceptable for depot throughput. Vendor RST CLI requires signed binary and can't be bundled in TS without validation.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- Short-term: Add conditional detection step to TS that checks for RST header and runs targeted wipe (sgdisk/Intel tool) only when detected. Create a signed wrapper script for the vendor tool and pilot in staging.
- Medium-term: Update depot acceptance checklist to require drive zeroing on RMA returns or include a fast header-clear step in depot intake.
- Long-term: Enhance our asset tracking to flag drives from consumer-origin repairs to route to a separate rapid-clean queue.

Requested action: Eng help to review and approve inclusion of signed Intel RST clear utility in our signed WinPE image. Also want SCCM/TS authoring guidance to implement detection-and-clear step safely.

Attachments: SMSTS logs, sample drive hex dump (first 4k), helper script in GH PR.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:24 - Luis Ortega: I'm taking ownership. Reproduced on a lab drive. Confirmed the RST header lives at sector 64 and blocks DiskPart clean. Attaching sample hex dump.
2026-03-11 14:12 - Depot Ops (Maya Chen): We saw 7 devices overnight with same symptom; manual sg_discard/sgdisk fixed them but throughput suffers. Will hold further batches until we have a script.

2026-03-12 10:03 - Eng (Marco Silva): Reviewed logs. Adding a conditional PowerShell/WinPE step that runs 'dd' equivalent to zero sector 64 if header matches pattern. Need approved signed binaries. Asking Security for sign-off (ticket INT-247100 created).
2026-03-13 08:45 - Security (Priya Nair): We need an audit for third-party vendor tool inclusion. If using our own sgdisk build, must be reproducible and built in CI.
resolution: Workaround implemented: imaging task sequence updated in staging to detect RST header and run targeted sector-zero on sector 64 using approved sgdisk build. Full rollout pending Security sign-off and CI build artifact. Follow-up doc created on Confluence.
